base.name: Whole Grains & Millets
base.detail: Ragi (finger millet), Foxtail millet (Thinai), Kodo millet (Varagu), whole wheat chapati, oats
base.benefit: High soluble fiber retards carbohydrate breakdown and stabilizes postprandial glucose

base.name: Pulses & Dhal
base.detail: Toor dhal sambar, moong dhal kootu, sprouted green gram, chana sundal, rajma
base.benefit: Plant protein and dietary fiber enhance satiety and curb insulin spikes

base.name: Vegetables & Greens
base.detail: Keerai (spinach/amaranth) poriyal, moringa (drumstick leaves), bitter gourd (pavakkai), ridge gourd, cabbage, beans
base.benefit: Micronutrients, polyphenols and near-zero glycemic impact

base.name: Healthy Hydration & Fermented
base.detail: Fresh buttermilk (mor with curry leaves and ginger), tender coconut water (moderate), rasam, lemon water
base.benefit: Aids digestion, cools metabolism and maintains electrolyte balance

non_veg.name: Lean Proteins
non_veg.detail: Country chicken breast (curry with less oil / grilled), steamed fish (nethili / vanjaram / rohu in light tamarind gravy)
non_veg.benefit: High biological value protein without saturated animal fat

egg.name: Eggs
egg.detail: Boiled eggs or egg-white vegetable omelette with black pepper and onions
egg.benefit: Rich in choline, protein, and zero glycemic impact

foods_to_limit.name: Polished White Rice & Normal Dosa/Idli
foods_to_limit.detail: Limit white ponni rice to 1 small cup; cap regular idli to 2-3 pieces or dosa to 1-2 thin dosas.
foods_to_limit.reason: High glycemic index quickly converts to simple glucose in bloodstream

foods_to_limit.name: Coconut Chutney & Heavy Oil Tadka
foods_to_limit.detail: Limit to 1 tablespoon; substitute with tomato-onion or mint-coriander chutney.
foods_to_limit.reason: Saturated fat density when consumed in high volume

foods_to_limit.name: Sweetened Filter Coffee & Tea
foods_to_limit.detail: Restrict to 1 small cup daily with zero sugar or minimal cow milk.
foods_to_limit.reason: Frequent tea/coffee sugar loads spike daily caloric and insulin burden

foods_to_limit.name: High-sugar Fruits
foods_to_limit.detail: Limit mangoes, sapota (chikoo), jackfruit and grapes to tiny occasional portions.
foods_to_limit.reason: Fructose density raises blood glucose when taken without fiber

foods_to_avoid.name: Traditional South Indian Sweets
foods_to_avoid.detail: Mysore pak, laddu, gulab jamun, jangiri, semiya payasam, halwa
foods_to_avoid.danger: Extremely high refined white sugar and saturated ghee content

foods_to_avoid.name: Deep-Fried Street & Tiffin Items
foods_to_avoid.detail: Medu vada, bajji, bonda, samosa, pakoda, commercial potato chips
foods_to_avoid.danger: Trans fats and reheated oils aggravate insulin resistance and vascular strain

foods_to_avoid.name: Sugary & Carbonated Beverages
foods_to_avoid.detail: Commercial soft drinks, sweetened fruit juices, condensed milk beverages, energy drinks
foods_to_avoid.danger: Liquid simple sugars absorb immediately and trigger acute glucose spikes

foods_to_avoid.name: Ultra-Processed Bakery Items
foods_to_avoid.detail: Maida parotta, white bread, cream biscuits, pastries, puffs
foods_to_avoid.danger: Refined flour (maida) strips digestive fiber and promotes abdominal adiposity

healthy_eating_tips.title: The South Indian Healthy Plate Rule
healthy_eating_tips.desc: Fill 50% of your plate with cooked vegetables/greens (poriyal, kootu, salad), 25% with protein (dhal, sundal, eggs, fish), and only 25% with carbs (rice, chapati, idli).

healthy_eating_tips.title: 15-Minute Post-Meal Walk (Shatapawali)
healthy_eating_tips.desc: Take a gentle 10 to 15-minute walk within 30 minutes after major meals. This activates large leg muscles to pull glucose from the blood without demanding extra insulin.

healthy_eating_tips.title: Proper Water Timing
healthy_eating_tips.desc: Drink 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily. Avoid gulping large amounts during meals; drink a glass 30 minutes before eating to aid satiety and digestive fire.

healthy_eating_tips.title: Smart Carbohydrate Sequencing
healthy_eating_tips.desc: Eat fiber (salad/greens) and protein (dhal/egg/meat) FIRST, and rice/chapatis LAST. This significantly flattens post-meal glucose and insulin peaks.
